# Continue older Python sessions

Old conversations no longer need a blanket Python-state reset after upgrading from the replay-based `code` tool. Plain and compressed v1/v2 snapshots are converted on the next `code` call, then saved as interpreter checkpoints. Existing conversation messages and v3 checkpoints remain compatible.

The conversion restores saved variables, functions, and inputs using recorded tool results, errors, and denials. It does not repeat completed tool operations or ask for their approval again. Pending approvals can still resume after a restart. New requests execute normally instead of reusing old results.

## Filesystem compatibility

Old snapshots never stored the contents of direct filesystem reads. Conversion reads the current files through readonly mounts, matching the old runtime. A changed file can change a reconstructed value or make an old assertion fail. If reconstruction fails, the original snapshot is preserved and the error gives the specific cause. Ordinary chat remains available.

`reset=true` remains an explicit way to clear Python state. It is no longer required solely because a session has a v1/v2 snapshot. Incompatible helper type signatures or execution limits can still require a reset.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/mistrjirka/PiTTy/compare/v0.7.11...v0.7.12)
